shapeNotes.straight: one run on the backing wall, nothing else
shapeNotes.galley: two facing runs with a 1200 mm aisle: a run on the wall and a freestanding run opposite it with a finished back and closed ends (no stools)
shapeNotes.L: runs on the two walls of a 90 degree corner, joined at the corner
shapeNotes.U: an L plus a third run facing the first leg, joined to the back run
shapeNotes.peninsula: a run on the wall with a run reaching out from it at right angles; stools on its far side
shapeNotes.island: a run on the wall and a freestanding island parallel to it, stools on its far side

a pot rail with pans over the hob (potRail)

a fallen leaf by a plant

a cloth over the table, hanging in folds

signsNote: roll.mjs deals 2-3 signs per area from `signs` (only those whose `in` lists the area), each at most once in a home, so a home has at most one mug. Name them in the spec with Home.sign or by placing the asset.

plantPlaces.say: a pot on a window sill
a plant on a shelf or a cabinet top
herbs or a pot on the worktop
a hanging plant from a rail or hook
a floor plant (at most one in an area)

plantsNote: plants is how many; plantPlaces says where each one lives. An area gets distinct places, so at most one floor plant.
foregroundNote: Each area's near-camera piece comes from its own use first; a plant only when none of these fits.
accentNote: One warm accent per home, from terracotta, ochre, rust, sage, clay rose or honey: its hex goes to new Home({ accent }). Each area names the textile that carries it (accentOn); set tone: 'accent' on that piece (cushion, foldedThrow, cloth, tablecloth, teaTowel, benchCushion, floorCushion, runner, tableRunner, duvetCloth).

passages.say: pass-through (a hatch with its own counter under it; not walked through)
wide pass-through (a half-wall hatch with its own counter, 2000 mm wide)
portal (deep reveal, a step in the threshold)
pocket-door opening (door half slid into the wall)

passageNote: roll gives each arch an opening style from `passages`; a counter style (pass, widepass) is built with its own counter and is not a way through, so give it no `to`, or use the arch/cased kind for a connection. Style goes in the opening: { kind: 'arch', style, x }. A pass-through carries its own counter (worktop 400 mm into the room, a cabinet body under it): put no worktop or sideboard there and keep 600 mm of floor clear in front; a walk-through opening shows floor running on beyond and one thing of the next room (opening.hint: picture | rug | lamp | chair, else dealt from the position).

windows.say: two-sash window (the old kitchen's: thick frame, slightly open)
picture window (one large fixed pane, slim frame; 2100 x 1400 mm, sill 650)
tall pair (two tall narrow casements side by side, 1100 x 1800 mm, sill 450)
window wall (floor-level lights between slim mullions with a transom; 3800 x 2300 mm, sill 100; it takes the whole wall, so no other opening beside it)
bay window (three angled panes projecting 500 mm outside, a seat at the sill; 2400 x 1500 mm, sill 450; it takes the wall's middle, no other opening beside it)
french glass doors to the outside (two leaves ajar, 1500 x 2250 mm; keep 1000 x 1500 mm of floor clear in front)
sliding glass doors to the outside (two panels, one half slid, 2400 x 2250 mm; keep the floor in front clear)

windowsNote: roll gives each window a style from `windows`; at most one wall, bay, french or slider per area, and a window with sash 'fixed' (over a sink) stays a two-sash window. Style goes in the opening: { kind: 'window', style: 'picture' | 'pair' | 'wall' | 'bay', x } or { kind: 'door', style: 'french' | 'slider', x }; width, height and sill default from the style (opening.js STYLE). A glass door or wall of glass counts as an opening for the 1200 mm of clear wall rule, and its sheet of daylight lights the area.

boardPlaces.say: flat on the worktop with a loaf, knife and a few vegetables on it
on the breakfast table, with bread or cheese on it
hanging from a rail or hook by its hole
two boards stacked on the worktop
leaning against the wall (the old way, at most one home in five)

lightNote: area.light is the one lamp of the area. pendant: hang a.table(...).over('pendantLamp') (or over an island or a chair) so it reads in the home view; the roll deals one in most kitchens, dining areas and reading corners, so a pendant is a decision, not an extra. If the lamp would overlap the window in the home view, slide it along the table (over('pendantLamp', { dx })) rather than dropping it.

island.say: a kitchen island facing the neighbour (the kitchen's shape is island)

peninsula.say: a kitchen peninsula reaching toward the neighbour (the kitchen's shape is peninsula)

sofaBack.say: a sofa or armchair with its back to the neighbour

openShelf.say: an open shelf unit seen from both sides

rug.say: a rug whose edge lies on the seam

hangingLight.say: a hanging light over the dining table, which stands by the seam

halfWall.say: a half wall about 1000 mm high

floorChange.say: a floor change: tiles in one area and boards beyond, in one straight line by the other separator

openPlan.note: roll.mjs deals openPlan (about 2 homes in 5 with at least two joinable areas). chain = the joined areas in order, layout row (one long back wall) or corner (turns 90 degrees at seam `turn`), seams[i].separators (at least one furniture) and overlap mm. Each joined area's `backing` is set so no side wall stands on a seam. See openplan.mjs and compose.mjs H.join.

stillLife.note: For each waist-high top the roll deals 2 or 3 of its things (never a cloth, runner or rug: those are not things) and one wall arrangement for the longest bare wall stretch (check-home 'bare': a top over 0.4 m2 holds two things at least; no wall stretch over 1.8 m is empty between 1.0 and 2.0 m high). Put each thing on its top with a.onTop slots so nothing overlaps or overhangs.

wall: open shelf with plates and jars (openShelf)
pot rail with pans over or beside the hob (potRail)
spice rack on the wall by the hob (spiceRack)

wall shelf over the sideboard, its bottom 400-600 over the top (wallShelf)

motion.note: Living, moving things dealt per area by motion-roll.mjs (read there and in src/motion/index.js). Each kind: say (plain words), needs (openWindow: the area has a window or glass door rendered open; plant: the area has a plant), in (area kinds), weight. flies: it passes through the opening, so that window is opened wide enough (rules.js VISITOR_OPEN); a number (the bird: 800) is the narrowest window in mm it can use, and the roll deals it only to an area with a window that wide. Count: how many kinds one area gets (never the same kind twice). Add a kind here, in src/motion/<kind>.js and in the PLUGINS map of src/motion/index.js.

wind.say: a plant stirs in a breeze from the open window

butterfly.say: a butterfly drifts in through the open window, wanders, perches, and leaves again

bee.say: a bee buzzes in through the open window, darts about, lands on a plant or the sill, and leaves again

bird.say: a small bird flies in through the wide open window, perches on the sill or a cabinet top, looks about, and leaves again

cat.say: a cat asleep, curled on a sofa, bed, chair, rug or the floor, breathing slowly

paw.say: a cat's paw reaches out from behind the curtain, searching, and goes back
